char.mentor.name: The Mentor
char.businessman.name: The Businessman
char.editor.name: The Editor
char.reformist.name: The Reformist
char.aide.name: The Aide
card.act0_appointment_day.text: Your mentor finds you right after the oath, a hand on your shoulder. "Congratulations. People expect things from someone in your position now — starting with your first words to the press."
card.act0_constituent_land_case.text: A family from your district writes to you: compensation for land taken by a public project was calculated three different ways in three different documents. They are not asking for money. They are asking which number is real.
card.act0_constituent_land_case.right: Forward it to the local office.
card.act0_first_parliament_speech.text: Your first scheduled address to the chamber. Two drafts sit on your desk — one proposes transparent complaint procedures, the other demands harsher punishment for the officials named in last month's scandal.
card.act0_first_parliament_speech.right: Demand harsher punishment for the guilty.
card.act0_first_interview.text: The reporter catches you in the corridor, recorder already running. "One question. When the rules and senior people collide — which side are you on?"
card.act0_mentor_advice.text: "You have good instincts," your mentor says over tea. "But instincts don't pass votes. Relationships do. Build them first. Reform later — from a position where your refusal costs them something."
card.act0_private_dinner_invitation.text: An envelope with no letterhead. A private dinner: eight names, three of which you have only ever seen on television. No agenda is mentioned. *None is needed.*
card.act1_committee_opportunity.text: "The Budget Oversight seat opens next week," your mentor says. "The selection process is a formality — *if the right person mentions your name.* Shall I?"
card.act1_businessman_intro.text: At a reception, your mentor steers a man in a quiet, expensive suit toward you. "We fund what governments are too slow to fund," the man says. "*And I admire people who move faster than their institutions.*"
card.act1_businessman_glimpse.text: Two receptions later, you see him again — the quiet, expensive suit, laughing at something a deputy from the appropriations committee has said. A fragment drifts past: "…went through last week. I won't forget it." He does not look your way.
card.act1_business_permit.text: "One permit," the businessman says. "Environmental compliance — approved once, resubmitted after a form change, sitting on someone's desk for five months. Nothing illegal. Just gravity. *You could remove the gravity.*"
card.act1_business_permit.left: Let the process run its course.
card.act1_constituent_case_callback.text: The complete file arrives, heavier than expected. The audit confirms it: three valuations, two signatures that don't match, and one official who has since been promoted. Your aide waits by the door, her notes already clipped to the cover.
card.act1_editor_profile_offer.text: The editor's office smells of coffee and fresh proofs. "We're running a series on the new generation in politics. You would open it. Good photos, better questions — and I choose the questions."
card.act1_reformist_bill_intro.text: "Procurement disclosure," the Reformist says, sliding a draft across your desk. "Every contract above the threshold, published within thirty days. Half the chamber will hate it — the important half."
card.act1_staff_hiring.text: Your aide flags one CV in the pile. "The committee vice-chair's nephew. Genuinely qualified — he'd top my shortlist even without the name. *But the name is on it.*"
card.act1_local_project.text: The district's drainage system has failed twice this month. Normal review takes a season the district doesn't have. Your committee seat can move it to the top of the queue — one signature, entirely within your authority.
card.act1_mentor_vote_request.text: "The committee elects its secretary on Thursday," your mentor says. "Vote for my candidate. Reliable. Knows how things are done." A pause. "*I don't ask often.*"
card.act1_small_reform_success.text: Your amendment passes — small, procedural, genuinely useful. Complaint response deadlines are now binding. In the corridor, the cameras find you.
card.act1_business_dinner.text: A private room above the city. The businessman orders without opening the menu. Toward the end of the evening, the waiter hovers with the bill, uncertain where to set it down.
card.act1_minor_rumor.text: "It's small," your aide says, phone in hand. "A forum thread claims your committee seat was arranged. Two hundred comments so far. It's wrong on the details — mostly."
card.act1_minor_rumor.right: Ask the Editor for clarifying coverage.
card.act1_committee_result_supported.tex: "The vote went through," your aide reports. "Your mentor's candidate is committee secretary now. He asked me to pass along that the agenda office will always find room for your items."
card.act1_committee_result_refused.text: "The vote went through anyway," your aide says. "Without you. The new secretary read the agenda this morning — your two items moved from Thursday to 'pending review.'"
card.act1_reformist_warning.text: The Reformist falls into step beside you. "You get things done. I've noticed — everyone has. Efficiency is useful. It also becomes a habit very quickly, and *habits get inherited by people worse than you.*"
card.act1_first_promotion.text: The call comes on a Tuesday: deputy chair of the committee. The official letter cites your legislative record. *The unofficial version depends on who is telling it.*
